extracted.intended_audience: regulatory commenters, policy advocates, agency counsel, and scholars interested in OIRA review and notice-and-comment strategy
extracted.subtask_description: Drafting public comments to agencies with the explicit goal of influencing OIRA's interagency review by supplying high‑quality analytic critique (especially cost‑benefit analysis), suitable formatting, and—where appropriate—direct engagement with OIRA staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include usable cost-benefit analysis (CBA) content
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment include cost-benefit analysis content of a quality OIRA can use?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIRA's mandate focuses on regulatory analysis quality; comments that 'address CBA deficiencies' speak OIRA's language. Provide analytically rigorous critique (not just assertions): corrected estimates, omitted benefit categories, alternative valuations, sensitivity ranges, and clear presentation of methods and data so OIRA can incorporate or rely on the critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify deficiencies in the agency's RIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment identify deficiencies in the agency's RIA?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about flaws (e.g., omitted benefit categories, incorrect baseline, methodological errors). Pointing out concrete analytical mistakes or omissions makes the comment actionable for OIRA reviewers, who routinely probe RIA quality and may press agencies to revise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propose alternative analytical assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment propose alternative analytical assumptions (discount rates, baselines)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest explicit alternative assumptions (different discount rates, counterfactual baselines, mortality/morbidity valuations, compliance rates), justify them, and show how results change under those assumptions. OIRA responds to substantive alternative analyses rather than mere disagreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify impacts the agency may have under-estimated
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment quantify impacts the agency may have under-estimated?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quantified estimates (point estimates and ranges) of benefits, costs, or other impacts the agency missed or undervalued. Use transparent methods and data sources; show sensitivity and likely magnitude so OIRA can assess materiality and request revisions if warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider direct engagement with OIRA during review
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the commenter consider directly engaging OIRA during interagency review?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sophisticated commenters meet directly with OIRA staff during the review period; OIRA logs reflect substantial parallel engagement. For significant rules, include direct outreach as part of a complete strategy (meetings, memos). Note: direct engagement is a distinct channel from formal notice-and-comment and can amplify analytic points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format for quick extraction by OIRA staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the comment formatted so OIRA staff can extract the analytical points quickly?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure comments to highlight key analytical critiques up front (executive summary, numbered points, clear labeling of assumptions and numbers). Concise presentation, prominently displayed calculations, tables, and highlighted conclusions make it easier for OIRA to spot and act on the issues you raise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft substantive agency comments because they often reach OIRA
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment to the agency assume it will be forwarded to OIRA (i.e., is it substantive enough for OIRA)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive comments to the agency typically are forwarded to OIRA when the rule enters interagency review. Treat a well-crafted agency comment as also addressing OIRA: include analytical content and formatting that will be useful to OIRA reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize OIRA engagement for 'significant' rules (EO 12866 threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the rule 'significant' (e.g., $100M+ annual effects or otherwise meeting EO 12866 criteria) so that OIRA engagement is likely to be useful?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIRA engagement yields most leverage for significant rules. For non-significant rules, the agency's response is the primary leverage point. Use the EO 12866 thresholds (including the $100M annual effects benchmark) to decide whether to invest in analytic work and direct OIRA outreach.
